items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Norman Granz in the context of the Jazz at the Philharmonic tours ('That's when Norman Granz came along') and discusses working with Charlie Parker, but does not describe a direct personal or professional relationship with Granz himself, other than being aware of his involve

ctx.x: Okay, I want to get back to Charlie Parker playing and recording with you. Do you remember the first time you met Parker?

Well, the first day -- the first time, I really don't know exactly where that I met Parker. I know that (inaudible), the first time I met Parker was on 52nd Street. What was the name of that club there? I was playing at this, and I went to listen to the -- there was Brown on the bass. They had a white piano player. There was Charlie Parker, Dizzy Gillespie and the drummer with this -- what was the name of this guy?

items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: Norman Granz came, and he had the band. And he said, man, I want to record this band. He came to me to -- would you like to record for me... Then he had Flip Phillips and they contract with a jazz trombonist -- Charlie Parker -- so they brought Charlie to the Palladium.

ctx.x: Right. Because I want to get into your involvement, the Afro-Cuban's involvement with the Afro-Cuban jazz scene starting around the time of '46-47.
That's when Norman Granz came along with the (inaudible).
Uh-huh. Can you talk about that involvement with Granz? What was that (inaudible)?
